name: Rafał Dzadzamira-Sørby
location: Deepwell Station — lives in McKinley Flats in a modest building with structural damp he has stopped reporting, near sub-level access near Dearborn and Jackson
description:
Rafał is thickset and weathered, with the specific bodily competence of someone who lifts heavy things in bad conditions for a living. His skin is mid-brown and perpetually flushed, his hair a faded reddish-brown that he keeps pulled back under a work cap. He smells, faintly and always, of the disinfectant compounds used in medical waste processing — a smell that precedes him and that he no longer notices at all, though those around him do. He has a single geneware modification: a gene-tweaked set of enhanced scent glands that he had installed for purely practical reasons (early detection of dangerous biological contamination), which has the side effect of making him an uncommonly attentive reader of a room's emotional atmosphere in ways he cannot fully articulate but acts on instinctively.

Rafał has been collecting the city's biological refuse for sixteen years. He moves through Meridian 88's medical ecosystem like a shadow — present at every clinic, every hospital loading bay, every back-alley surgical setup, invisible and indispensable. He has seen things disposed of that should have been reported. He has seen labels that don't match contents. He has seen waste streams from addresses that don't appear in any city directory. He is not, by temperament, an activist or an investigator. He is a man who goes to work, comes home, watches old footage of Polish basketball leagues that no longer exist, and tries not to think too hard about what he has seen. He is not entirely successful at this.

core_fears: Being pulled into something that ends his ability to work and support himself
That the things he has witnessed make him implicated simply by knowing
core_desires: A clean conscience about what he has seen
To be regarded as a person and not furniture by the medical professionals on his route
coping_mechanisms: Compartmentalization into routine — the manifests are filed, the route is run, it is someone else's problem to understand
Old sports footage as emotional reset
blind_spots: Underestimates how much he has absorbed and retained — he knows far more than he thinks he knows
Believes that because he has never actively wronged anyone, he bears no responsibility for what he has witnessed
psychology.secret: He has kept a private logbook — physical, hidden at home — noting irregularities in waste streams over the past six years. Address discrepancies, label mismatches, biological material disposed of under false categories. He started it as a kind of anxious accounting, telling himself he'd know what to do with it eventually. He does not know what to do with it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Plain and direct, working-class Meridian 88 vernacular with Polish-Zimbabwean idiom showing in his rhythm — phrases like 'that is what it is' functioning as punctuation for things he finds troubling
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, flat, slightly deliberate — the speech of someone who is used to not being listened to and has stopped performing urgency
verbal_tics: 'That is what it is' for things he finds troubling
Prefacing uncertain information with 'I only drive the truck'
example_lines: 'I only drive the truck. What's in the containers, that's — that is what it is. I sign the manifest, the manifest says what it says.'
'You're asking me if I noticed something. I notice things. I don't know what they mean. That's a different job and it's not mine.'

story_hooks: His private irregularity logbook contains an address that has been generating unregistered biological waste for over a year — he has no idea what is happening there and is terrified to find out, but equally terrified to keep sitting on the information.

A medical waste container he collected from a clinic in the Narrows contained material that, based on his enhanced scent detection, was recently alive. He processed it according to manifest. He has not stopped thinking about it.
narrative_function: Crucial civilian information source — knows where every medical facility's waste comes from and has a supernaturally good nose for when something is wrong. Reluctant witness. Represents the invisible labor that holds the city's infrastructure together.
augmentations: Enhanced scent glands (geneware — installed for occupational early-detection purposes). Reinforced lumbar support implant (workers' compensation, after a 2193 back injury). UBC supplement card for the months his contracts don't pay on time, which is most months.
daily_life: Up at four-thirty to catch the first Ferrogate Transit run to Deepwell Station, first pickup by six, works until two or three in the afternoon across his route, then processes manifests and disposal logs at home before whatever passes for an evening.
affiliation: Independent contractor — holds service contracts with four clinics, two pharmacies, and Aurochs Medical Complex peripheral disposal

decision_rules: Do the job correctly and document it — the documentation is protection
Don't volunteer information to people who haven't asked the right question
escalation_ladder: Admitting he has noticed something without specifying what
Producing the logbook — the absolute last resort

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Polite, low-key, gives nothing away — has learned that being invisible on the job is safer
interpersonal_modes.friends: Comfortable, dry, genuinely warm; enjoys being fed and will talk about basketball for hours

stress_responses.low: Becomes slightly more talkative as displacement
stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet; starts doing unnecessary small physical tasks — checking latches, refolding things
stress_responses.high: A very specific stillness, and then a decision — he is not a man who escalates gradually, he makes a threshold choice

contradictions: Claims he doesn't want to be involved in anything larger than his route while meticulously documenting the very things that would involve him
Performs lack of curiosity while noticing and retaining everything
habits: Eats lunch in his vehicle alone, always, regardless of weather
Leaves a weekly data-offering for the E.L.F. he calls The Incinerator — a grim but honest name, he thinks
breaking_points: Discovering that something in his waste stream was a person
Being asked to falsify a manifest by a contractor he depends on financially

timeline.event: Born in McKinley Flats to a Polish-Zimbabwean couple; father a waste processing worker, mother a transit maintenance worker
Began bio-waste disposal contracting after a decade in general waste infrastructure
Back injury on the job; lumbar implant installed via workers' compensation; payout dispute lasted eleven months
Began keeping private irregularity logbook after the first address discrepancy that troubled him enough to write down
